findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate by a datetime key, which is the only way the audit-log endpoint uses it
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"`. `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, "datetime")`, which is a `datetime`, so it raises `TypeError` as soon as `build_cursor` computes the next/prev cursor. `value_from_cursor` also returns `cursor.value` as a raw integer instead of converting it back to a datetime, as `DateTimePaginator` does. Any request with a non-zero cursor would therefore compare the `datetime` column to an integer in SQL. The `?optimized_pagination=true` path is broken on the first page and on every later page. The class apparently copies `Paginator` instead of `DateTimePaginator` and was never exercised.

findings.title: Negative-offset slice on a Django QuerySet raises instead of paginating; justifying comments are wrong
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`. A user-supplied cursor such as `0:-5:0` (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets) therefore produces a 500. The comments are wrong on two counts. "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing" is false. "This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" does not apply, because the slice does not become a valid read of earlier rows. This feature is exposed to superusers and global-access members, so it is a crash path in new code, not an optimization.

findings.title: `organization_context.member` dereferenced eagerly for every request, can raise AttributeError on the default path
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated for every request, even when `optimized_pagination` is not set. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is Optional. It is `None` for non-member access, such as org-auth-token requests where `request.user` is anonymous and `is_superuser` is False. Those requests now fail with `AttributeError` (500) on an endpoint that previously worked. The check should be computed only when `use_optimized` is true, and it should guard against `member is None`.

findings.title: Clamping negative offsets in the shared BasePaginator makes cursors inconsistent for all paginators
findings.body: `BasePaginator.get_result` is inherited by many endpoints. The change silently clamps a negative offset to 0 for the query, but `build_cursor` still receives the original cursor with the negative offset. `_build_next_values` and `_build_prev_values` compute `next_offset = offset + limit` from that negative value. The returned page therefore does not match the cursors that follow it, causing skipped or duplicated rows. Previously a negative offset failed loudly in Django. The comment "the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions" is incorrect, and `is_prev` cursors still pass the negative offset straight through to the slice. This behavior change to a shared class has nothing to do with the spans buffer.

findings.title: Redirect-chain depth limit silently reduced 10x and explanatory comment removed
findings.body: The loop bound changes from `0, 10000` to `0, 1000`, and the comment explaining the limit is deleted. This is unrelated to the eviction work in the PR. Span trees whose redirect chains are deeper than 1000 will now stop resolving early and fail to merge into the correct segment. That produces split segments, and it is not mentioned in the title or description.

findings.title: Switching segment storage from Redis SET to ZSET with no migration will hit WRONGTYPE on existing keys
findings.body: Segment keys `span-buf:s:*` change from sets (`SADD`/`SSCAN`/`SCARD`/`SUNIONSTORE`) to sorted sets (`ZADD`/`ZSCAN`/`ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE`). On deploy, buffers already in Redis are still plain sets, with TTL up to `redis_ttl` (1h). `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, `ZUNIONSTORE` and `ZSCAN` on them will return WRONGTYPE. This causes consumer errors, and flushes of in-flight segments will fail. Nothing handles or documents the transition, such as a new key prefix or draining first.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE uses default SUM aggregation, corrupting scores of duplicate members
findings.body: Scores are `end_timestamp_precise`, and the eviction via `zpopmin` relies on them as an ordering. `ZUNIONSTORE` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so a payload that exists in both `set_key` and `span_key` (or `parent_key`) gets its score doubled. A span redelivered after a consumer restart is one such case. The span then looks far newer than it is, so ordering is wrong and the wrong spans are evicted. Use `AGGREGATE MAX` (or `MIN`).

findings.title: max_segment_spans is now dead config and the cap is hard-coded to a different value in Lua
findings.body: The span-count check in `_load_segment_data` was removed, but `max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is still a constructor argument and attribute and is now unused. The real cap is the hard-coded `1000` in `add-buffer.lua`, which does not match the 1001 default and cannot be configured. Eviction also discards the oldest spans without emitting any metric or log, so operators can no longer see that segments are being truncated. The old `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric is gone.

findings.title: No test covers the new eviction behavior or the new paginator/endpoint code
findings.body: The PR's headline feature is evicting spans beyond 1000 per segment inside the Lua script (`zpopmin` on lowest score), and its correctness depends on the score ordering and the union count logic. The tests only add `end_timestamp_precise` to existing fixtures. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans and checks which ones survive, or that eviction works across merged sub-segments. There are also no tests for `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the `optimized_pagination` endpoint path, or the BasePaginator offset clamping. The datetime-key bug and the member-None bug would have been caught by even a basic test.

findings.title: Comment claims Cursor allows negative offsets for reverse pagination, but nothing implements or supports that
findings.body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for "efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions", yet no code changed. `int(offset)` already accepted negatives, and downstream consumers (Django slicing, `build_cursor`) do not support them. The comment misleads future readers into thinking negative offsets are a supported, safe feature.
